dsDescriptionValue.value:
The ETCBC database of the Hebrew Bible, contains the scholarly text of the Hebrew Bible with linguistic markup.
A previous version, Hebrew Text Database ETCBC4, can be found in EASY (see the link below). See the description there for more details.

The present dataset is a new version:

(A) the content has been updated, all features have been filled in for all objects whenever applicable;
(B) not all feature values have been checked; for that we have to wait for version 4c.

The reason to submit this version now is the upcoming Annual Meeting of the Society of Biblical Literature (November 21-24, 2015, Atlanta).

value:
The ETCBC4b text is based on the printed edition of the Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia, editio quinta emendata (1997).
This edition, published by the German Bible Society, represents the text found in the oldest complete manuscript of the Hebrew Bible / Old Testament, the so-called Codex Leningradensis (Codex Firkovich B 19 A).
Although it cannot be taken for granted that this manuscript, and hence the scholarly edition that represents it, always contains the best (“original”) reading and although we have older manuscripts for various parts of the Bible (Dead Sea Scrolls, some other codices that cover only part of the Hebrew Bible), taking this edition as basis for the electronic text was a natural step because of its central role as *the* scholarly edition of the Old Testament that is almost exclusively used by biblical scholars and that is the basis for almost all Bible translations in modern languages as far as they translate the Hebrew text.

The linguistic features of ETCBC4b have been provided by the Eep Talstra Centre for Bible and Computing.
At the moment of depositing, this version is still in beta.
The data deposited is the newest data that was available at the date of depositing.

This LAF resource has been generated from the contents of an Emdros database

However, not all data that the ETCBC group is producing, is published in this form.
We have made a selection of some extra data, and have added that as an extra LAF annotation file, which can be used in conjunction with the LAF resource originating from the Emdros database.
We refer to the ETCBC organization on Github for more examples of work done on with LAF-Fabric operating on ETCBC4.
